findings.message: apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts arriveRumor / apps/server/src/intel.ts RumorBook.decided: a decided (player, request id) is replayed regardless of the type in the new request, so a retried id naming a different type gets the earlier type's decision and lead resent, unlike the ledger's own contract (a reused id for another item is 'duplicate'). The browser always sends fresh ids, so there is no player-facing impact today; worth aligning before economy-online's shop reuses this purchase path.

Acceptance item 5 of features/intel-online/game-task.md says no raw frame may carry a source's, cache's or unseen ship's position. In tests/integration/intel.test.ts ('sends every lead and answer only to its player...', lines 466-484), the raw-frame scan only looks for other players' session ids and rubbing ids. Positions are checked only indirectly: each received lead is parsed with the strict journalMessageSchema (headlessClient stores leads undecoded, so an extra field would fail), the status map holds only the player's own key, and the status journal must equal room.journalOf. Unseen ships are checked only through the stranger never receiving the fighters' ids. This does catch a position leaking through the new intel channels, but no raw state frame is searched for source or cache coordinates. That is weaker than the wording, not a missing test.

# Decisions: intel-online-review

From the operator session of 2026-09-26, decided by the assistant under the operator's standing instruction and recorded in `operator-logs/decisions-overnight.md` (#59).

## Decisions

- intel-online-001 passed every check. Its two reviewers stopped at 18:19 UTC on 2026-09-25 without a verdict, because the account's weekly usage limit was reached. The review deadline expired at 19:18. md-manager's runbook says a reviewer blocked this way needs a new run for a fresh review.
- This run restores the exact verified snapshot (`bc53558`) and changes nothing, so the reviewers see the same code that passed verification.
- The five P2 notes carried from `fruit-kits-online` stay in intel-online's task. They were already implemented in the snapshot, and the reviewers check them.

## Assumptions

- Everything in `features/intel-online/` stands.

## Deferred

- `economy-online` (with the hold-grace playtest fix as its first item) comes next.

concerns.message: The restore excludes only `features/`, so it quietly assumes this run's base (7edbe33) matches intel-online-001's base (24d7ab1 plus its feature-file commits) everywhere outside `features/`. The recent commit messages suggest only feature files changed, but nothing in the task checks this. The worker's `git diff --stat refs/workflow/.../game -- . ':!features'` check can't catch it either, because it compares against the snapshot, not against the base.
concerns.consequence: If anything outside `features/` landed on main between the two bases, the restore would silently revert it. The run would still pass as 'unchanged', and the reviewers would approve a tree that undoes that change.

concerns.message: The task relies on `refs/workflow/cf66e7124fc568c7/game` still existing and pointing at bc53558. That ref belongs to the finished run 001, so cleanup of that run could remove it. Refs are shared across worktrees, but the worker can't recover if the ref is gone. The task names the commit but never tells the worker to check that the ref resolves to it.
concerns.consequence: If the ref was pruned, the restore fails and the run stops as blocked. If the ref was moved, the worker would restore a tree other than the verified snapshot, and the diff check would still pass because it compares against the same ref.

concerns.message: 'Any check fails → blocked, don't fix' leaves no room for a single retry of a flaky browser or integration test. This is a shared machine, and the suite has 13 two-browser scenarios on a 1800 s budget and an integration suite on a 300 s budget. A timing flake under load is plausible and says nothing about the code.
concerns.consequence: One transient failure pauses the run for the operator, even though the code is identical to a snapshot that already passed. That costs another operator round-trip on a feature whose review deadline has already expired once.

concerns.message: The policy's `rumor-journal` description says the journal opens with Tab, but the implemented design (intel-online game-task, item 8) uses M. The acceptance there records this, but the fresh reviewers get the policy and PRD (§8 says Tab for journal and map) as context and may not read that note.
concerns.consequence: A reviewer could flag the key mismatch as a defect and block approval of an unchanged snapshot, which would force yet another run.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Skip the worker's restore step. Have the controller create the `game` lane branch directly with bc53558's tree for everything outside `features/` (for example with `git read-tree`/`commit-tree`, or by cherry-picking the snapshot on top of 7edbe33), then send it straight to the verifier and the fresh reviewers. The worker adds nothing a mechanical tree copy doesn't already do, and removing it removes a window where an agent could 'fix' something.
challenge.cheap_experiment: Before any worker starts, run from the repo (read-only, a few seconds): (1) `git rev-parse refs/workflow/cf66e7124fc568c7/game` and check that it prints bc53558…; (2) `git diff --stat 24d7ab1 7edbe33 -- . ':!features'` and check that it prints nothing (the base hasn't drifted outside `features/`); (3) `git diff --name-only 7edbe33 bc53558 -- . ':!features'` and check that every path falls under the policy's `owned_paths`. If (2) is not empty, the restore would revert real changes, and the plan should switch to a merge of the snapshot on top of the base.

scenarios.description: One browser creates a private match from the landing page; the HUD shows the code, the protocol version, one player and a connected status.
Two browsers join the same private match with their ships in sight of each other; one sails with the keyboard and the other browser's view shows that ship at the new server-authoritative position.
A browser sails its ship around a shoal to an island dock with the keyboard and docks there; the HUD shows the dock and the ship stops at it.
Two browsers in one match with their ships out of sight of each other: neither view lists or draws the other ship until one sails within the sight radius, and it disappears again when it sails away.

One browser opens a practice duel against the dummy, lands a jab and then a keyboard throw (J then K a frame apart); the dummy's health bar and the HUD drop by the move data's damage, and hitboxes can be shown.

Two browsers: one creates a duel, the other joins by its code; after the countdown the first lands a strike on the second, and both views show the same authoritative health, round clock and result, with the connection line showing input delay and corrections.

Two browsers in one match are placed within grapple range; the host sails at the guest and presses J; both see the grapple telegraph, then a three-second countdown and the arena; the duel is decided; the winner returns to the sea with protection shown, and the loser sees a respawn countdown and then their ship at a dock.

Two browsers moored at different islands each hold E and collect a different rubbing type; the host grapples the guest at sea, wins the duel by tapping attack keys, and picks the guest's type within five seconds; the host's HUD shows both types and more gold, the guest's shows the loss.

Two browsers: the host starts a private match from the lobby, both see the ready countdown and the match timer; the host collects both rubbing types, sees the full-set reveal and the route, sails to the final island's claim tile and holds E for ten seconds; both browsers show the results with the host as the winner.

Two browsers start a private match from the lobby with test-only short timings; nobody claims; the timer runs out; both browsers show the results with the no-winner deadline headline, and the route compass is shown inactive while no route is known.

One browser moored at an island opens its ruin with R and reads the clue from the page; the test derives the answer from the displayed clue only, submits it, sees '+40 gold' and the island unlocked, then holds E to collect the rubbing.

One browser moors at a pedestal's dock, presses F, reads the kit name from the panel, holds F for three seconds and sees its HUD show Ember; it grapples the second browser at sea, casts the flame bolt (U) in the arena, both browsers see the bolt drawn, and the second browser's health bar drops by the bolt's damage.

Two browsers start a private match; the host opens the journal with Tab and reads its start rumor (a type and an island or sector name) from the page, sails to a dock, moors, buys a targeted rumor and sees its gold drop by 25 and a new journal entry marked targeted; the guest's page never shows the host's rumors.
